parsed_answer.content: Consumer lag in Apache Kafka is the delta between the latest offset produced to a partition and the last offset committed by a consumer group. It is the primary indicator of system health in event-driven architectures, signaling that the consumer throughput is insufficient to keep pace with the producer's ingestion rate. When lag grows, it increases end-to-end latency, which can breach SLAs or cause stale data processing. Handling lag requires a multi-layered strategy: first, by optimizing consumer performance through batching and parallelization; second, by scaling the consumer group horizontally to match the partition count; and finally, by tuning Kafka-specific configurations like fetch.min.bytes and max.poll.records to balance throughput against memory pressure.

items: Partition Rebalancing: Adding consumers triggers a rebalance. Use Static Membership (group.instance.id) to avoid unnecessary rebalances during rolling restarts, which otherwise spikes lag.

Consumer Throughput Tuning: Adjust max.poll.records to ensure the processing time per batch stays well below the max.poll.interval.ms threshold to prevent the group coordinator from triggering a rebalance due to a perceived 'stuck' consumer.

Backpressure and Throttling: If the downstream sink (e.g., a database) is the bottleneck, implement a circuit breaker or rate-limiting to prevent the consumer from crashing due to OOM errors while trying to buffer records.
Monitoring: Use tools like Burrow or Prometheus/Grafana to track 'Consumer Lag' metrics via JMX. Alerts should be based on time-based lag (how many seconds behind) rather than just offset-based lag.

parsed_answer.content: A common production trap is assuming that adding more consumers than partitions will solve lag. It will not; the extra consumers will simply sit idle. If you are truly bottlenecked at the partition level, you must perform a partition expansion (re-keying or adding partitions), which is a high-risk operation that can disrupt message ordering guarantees. Always ensure your partition key strategy allows for sufficient parallelism before going live.
